concepts.title: Concept of Man Alive
concepts.section: Why the Novel Matters - Main Essay
concepts.definition: Human existence viewed as an integrated, vital whole encompassing body, mind, and spirit as one unified entity rather than isolated physical or mental components.
concepts.key_idea: True human life resides in the totality of the living person, not in separate abstract parts like soul or intellect.
question_patterns: explain D.H. Lawrence's concept of man alive
how does the author distinguish between man alive and bits of man
describe why the living body is central to Lawrence's philosophy
what marks animate things from inanimate objects in the essay
analyze the author's critique of spiritual and scientific views of humanity

solution_steps.explain: Lawrence asserts that human identity resides in the entirety of the living organism, termed 'man alive'.
He refutes scientists, philosophers, and clergy who reduce humans to isolated parts such as soul, mind, brain, or organs.
The complete living individual is greater than any individual constituent part.

concepts.title: Supremacy of the Novel
concepts.section: Why the Novel Matters - Main Essay
concepts.definition: The characterization of narrative fiction as the primary literary form capable of engaging and reflecting the entire living human being rather than fragmented aspects.
concepts.key_idea: The novel stands above science, philosophy, and poetry because it alone presents character and life in full wholeness.
question_patterns: why does the author consider the novel superior to philosophy and science
how does the novel reflect the wholeness of a human being
explain the phrase 'the novel is the one bright book of life'
contrast the scope of the novel with that of poetry and religion
what makes the novel uniquely capable of capturing dynamic life

solution_steps.action: examine the author's argument for fiction
solution_steps.explain: Philosophy and science focus on isolated thoughts or dead specimens, whereas the novel depicts living human beings in action.

solution_steps.action: evaluate the holistic nature of novels
solution_steps.explain: A novel presents characters whose physical, emotional, and moral life functions dynamically without rigid abstraction.

concepts.title: Tremulations on the Ether
concepts.section: Why the Novel Matters - Main Essay
concepts.definition: A metaphor describing written words and ideas as aerial vibrations that remain lifeless until received and vitalized by an active human reader.
concepts.key_idea: Textual messages are mere vibrations on ether; their value arises when they stimulate the whole living person.
question_patterns: what does the author mean by 'tremulations on ether'
explain 'the novel as a tremulation' in Lawrence's essay
how do written words achieve vitality according to Lawrence
describe the interaction between a book's message and 'man alive'
analyze how book tremulations differ between novels and philosophical texts

solution_steps.explain: Words in books are compared to radio waves or ether vibrations that travel across space.
These vibrations take on real life only when received by a living reader who quivers into fresh awareness.

concepts.title: Integrity versus Consistency
concepts.section: Why the Novel Matters - Main Essay
concepts.definition: The philosophical distinction between living personal authenticity (integrity) through continuous adaptation and dynamic change, versus static adherence to fixed behavioral rules (consistency).
concepts.key_idea: Living individuals maintain true integrity by changing fluidly, whereas forced consistency turns living people into dead patterns.
question_patterns: how does Lawrence reconcile inconsistency of behavior with integrity
explain the difference between moral consistency and human integrity
why does sticking to a fixed pattern make a character dead in a novel
discuss the relationship between dynamic change and emotional vitality
analyze why right and wrong are instincts of the whole consciousness

solution_steps.explain: People naturally experience shifting feelings and perspectives over time.

solution_steps.action: contrast dynamic integrity with rigid consistency
solution_steps.explain: Fixing oneself to a rigid ideal turns a person into an unliving object, whereas responding fluidly preserves vital integrity.

concepts.title: Intransitive Verbs and Complements
concepts.definition: Verbs that express complete action without taking a direct object, often followed by prepositional or adverbial phrases serving as complements.
concepts.key_idea: Intransitive verbs do not transfer action to an object and use optional complements to complete circumstantial context.
question_patterns: identify the intransitive verb in the given sentence
explain the function of a complement following an intransitive verb
determine whether the verb in the sentence takes a direct object
classify the prepositional phrase following the intransitive verb
analyze the structure of sentences containing intransitive verbs

solution_steps.explain: Observe if the verb transfers action to a noun phrase object.
Note prepositional phrases modifying time, place, or manner after the verb.

concepts.title: Copulas and Predicate Complements
concepts.definition: Linking verbs such as be, become, and seem that connect a subject to a noun phrase or adjective phrase acting as a predicate complement.
concepts.key_idea: A copula links the subject to a descriptor or identity phrase, which can be nominal or adjectival.
question_patterns: identify the copula verb in the sentence
determine the syntactic category of the complement after the copula
classify whether the complement is a noun phrase or an adjective phrase
explain the linking role of copular verbs like be, become, and seem
find examples of copulas with adjective phrase complements in the text

solution_steps.explain: Identify copular verbs such as forms of be, become, or seem.
Determine if the following phrase is an Adjective Phrase (AP) or Noun Phrase (NP).

concepts.title: Phonetic Realizations of Digraph 'ch'
concepts.definition: The pronunciation rules for the letter combination 'ch', which yields /k/ in words of Greek/Latin origin, /ʃ/ in French borrowings, and /tʃ/ in traditional English words.
concepts.key_idea: Etymology determines whether 'ch' is pronounced as a plosive /k/, affricate /tʃ/, or fricative /ʃ/.
question_patterns: what sound does 'ch' represent in words of Greek or Latin origin

identify words where 'ch' is pronounced as /k/ versus /tʃ/

explain why 'ch' before a consonant is pronounced /k/

solution_steps.action: examine word etymology or letter context
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the word originates from Greek/Latin (/k/), French (/ʃ/), or native English (/tʃ/).

concepts.title: Phonetic Realizations of Digraph 'gh'
concepts.definition: The pronunciation rules for 'gh', which renders /g/ word-initially, and either /f/ or silent in medial and word-final positions.
concepts.formula: gh_sound = initial(/g/) or non_initial(/f/ or silent)
concepts.key_idea: Initial 'gh' is always voiced /g/, while non-initial 'gh' alternates between /f/ and silent status.
question_patterns: how is initial 'gh' pronounced in English words
identify words where 'gh' is silent versus pronounced as /f/
classify the phonetic realization of 'gh' in given examples
explain the variation of 'gh' in word medial and final positions
group words according to whether 'gh' represents /g/, /f/, or no sound

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether 'gh' occurs at the beginning, middle, or end of the word.
Assign /g/ for initial position, and distinguish /f/ from silent for non-initial positions.
